items.text: Shamkhal Jafari, a commander of the Khatam al-Anbiya Air Defense Headquarters, announced that the headquarters will take actions against the enemy in the future that will cause surprise. He said the future behavior of this headquarters will confuse and astonish the enemy.
A video of two teenagers performing protest rap in Tehran metro has been released. In the song, the teenagers express their feelings and situation. They talk about freedom and prison in their lyrics.

Babak Dadbakhsh, a political prisoner in Ardabil prison, ended his hunger strike after promises from officials. He ended his strike on Wednesday, 10 Shahrivar, after receiving assurances regarding his demands. Dadbakhsh was transferred to the prison infirmary and is under observation.

Amir Hamidi, a national security expert, stated that the US is applying economic pressure, limiting revenues, and diplomatic pressure to change Tehran's cost-benefit calculation. He warned that the risk of escalation is high. Each stage of increased tension could lead to a heavier response for the Islamic Republic.

The Iranian national volleyball team defeated New Zealand 3-0 in their first match at the 2026 Asian Men's Championship. The sets ended with scores of 25-15, 25-12, and 25-22. Iran will face India in their second match on Sunday, 15 Shahrivar.

Saman Ghaderi, detained in connection with the December 1404 protests, was sentenced to 14 years in prison by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. He received 11 years for acting against national security and 3 years for insulting sacred beliefs. The sentence was communicated to him on Tuesday, 3 Shahrivar.
According to media reports, South Korea, under US pressure, is considering sending non-combat equipment to the vicinity of the Strait of Hormuz, although Seoul says no final decision has been made.

Leila Bahmani announced the development of a transitional justice program for the transition period. The program includes mechanisms to address human rights violations and examine the roles of individuals and institutions of the Islamic Republic. The planned components include a court, truth commission, investigation committee, and conditional amnesty.

A memorial birthday ceremony for Mehran Salimi was held on Thursday, 12 Shahrivar, at his gravesite. Mehran Salimi was 27 years old and was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Hashtgerd. A video of this ceremony was received by Iran International.

Parvaneh Salahshouri, former parliament member, criticized the economic and political situation and the execution of protesting youth. She said that the only thing people can endure anymore is death. She also questioned the double standards in handling protests.

Yisrael Katz stated that Israel will not withdraw from the security zone in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon. He considered the capture of the Ali Taher heights an important step in consolidating Israeli control over the area. The decision to capture these heights was made after discovering Hezbollah's command tunnels.

Hamidreza Haji Babaei, the deputy speaker of the parliament, said that the economic interests of the US in the region should be targeted and US bases should be hit. He also emphasized that US sanctions make Iran stronger. These remarks were made in response to US sanctions.

Saeed Bashirtash stated at the 'Free Iran and the European Union' conference that organizing political parties is important for the transition from the Islamic Republic. He added that parties can support people during protests. He also emphasized the necessity of strengthening parties for the post-Islamic Republic era.

A video shows that the establishment of a checkpoint in Pardis on the evening of Thursday, September 2, caused heavy traffic and inconvenience for people. This incident was reported by Iran International.

The Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon have become a key conflict point between Israel and Hezbollah. The area contains Hezbollah's underground infrastructure. The Islamic Republic has warned the US through Oman about Israel's capture of this area.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, stated that the nightly governmental gatherings will continue as long as Mojtaba Khamenei decides. He said the matter will not be closed based on others' opinions.

The grass field of Azadi Stadium has been completely removed and workers are preparing the base. Officials have announced that the football field will be usable by January. The previous grass was still usable, but a decision was made to replace it with hybrid grass.

Legal cases have been filed against several protesting nurses at Fayyazbakhsh Hospital in Tehran. The court sessions for six of them were held last week. Five nurses face charges including spreading false information and disturbing public opinion.

CENTCOM is investigating the causes of strikes in an American attack on Sirik county that killed four civilians, including a child. The US military will review archival drone and reconnaissance aircraft images and the targeting process. The investigation may examine misidentification, use of incomplete information, location errors, and human error.

Alireza Raisi, Deputy Minister of Health, warned about the increase in positive COVID-19 cases and called for intensified health precautions. In a letter to medical universities, he emphasized continuous monitoring of viruses causing acute respiratory diseases. He also recommended mask use in enclosed spaces and readiness of gathering centers to face the upcoming wave.

Rouhollah Rahimpour stated that Trump's remarks indicate Iran's nuclear activities are monitored by the US. He added that if Iran rebuilds its enrichment program, it would cross a red line for the US and Israel. In that case, the likelihood of a military attack on Iran's nuclear program would increase.

Reza Talebi reported that four missiles hit the site and one missile hit a nearby area in Sirik. He mentioned the high accuracy of the missiles and the possibility of errors in coordinates. He also referred to the UN Secretary-General's warning about humanitarian law compliance and the lack of a central warning system in Iran.

Tasnim reported that Kopal Nazemi refused to referee in the fifth week of the Premier League after Mooud Bonyadifard was selected to officiate the 107th derby. According to Tasnim, Nazemi expected to be assigned the Esteghlal vs Persepolis match and was upset after Bonyadifard was chosen. The refereeing committee had scheduled him for Malavan Bandar Anzali vs Nassaji Mazandaran, but he declined.

Israel Katz, Israel's defense minister, considered controlling the strategic heights of Ali Taher in southern Lebanon a key step to consolidate the Israeli army's presence. This decision was made after discovering Hezbollah's tunnel network. Israel will not withdraw until Hezbollah is fully disarmed and the threat to northern Israel is removed.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin stated that with the joining of China, Europe, and the Gulf Cooperation Council to the global campaign to sanction the Islamic Republic, regional media analyses about the fate of the war have changed. This change also includes media outlets that are opposed to the US and Israel.

Michael Owen spoke about his son James's eye condition that has caused his blindness. He explained that he needs to assist his son in situations like at restaurants and acts as his driver. Owen also mentioned that he spends more time with his son due to the illness and values their closer relationship.
A citizen stated in a video that their home heating package has been broken for four months and they cannot afford to repair it. They have to heat water in a barrel for their children to bathe.

Ahmad Khatami, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Tehran, said economic pressure aims to create a gap between the people and the system and weaken the front of truth. He added that these pressures have a long history and will ultimately lead to the defeat of the enemies. Khatami urged people to do whatever they can to help the Islamic Republic.

The IAEA has revealed new findings about Syria's undeclared nuclear program during Bashar al-Assad's era. The structure of Syria's nuclear reactor is very similar to North Korea's reactor. This reactor could have produced five to six kilograms of weapons-grade plutonium annually.

Ali Javid's sister joined the memorial campaign by lighting a candle in memory of her brother and nephew. Ali Javid, 38, and his 18-year-old daughter Shiva were killed in Mashhad. This incident occurred on January 8, 2026.

FC Barcelona surpassed one billion euros in annual revenue for the first time in the 2025-2026 fiscal year. Increased income from stadium use and sponsorships were key factors in this growth. The club hopes that a full return to Camp Nou will bring even more revenue.

Keyvan Khosravani, an Iranian artist and fashion designer, passed away at the age of 88 in France. He was influential in environmental art, architecture, and fashion design in Iran and designed clothes for Empress Farah Pahlavi. Khosravani was also a pioneer in men's boutique fashion in Iran.

Giorgia Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, has set a new record for the longest uninterrupted government in the country's republican history with 1413 days in office. The previous record was held by Silvio Berlusconi's second government. Meloni's government's stability is unprecedented in a country known for frequent government changes.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij organization, said the US must bow before the Iranian nation because it started the war. He described Israel as a war factory used to attack regional countries. Taeb also emphasized that Iran has never requested a ceasefire or negotiations.

Pouya Aideni, Iran's chess grandmaster, has decided to compete for France with the approval of the World Chess Federation. He cited unfulfilled promises and unpaid rewards by the Iranian Chess Federation as reasons for this decision. Aideni felt he had no choice but to change federations.

Israel's Defense Minister Yisrael Katz stated that Israel will not withdraw from the security zone in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon. He emphasized that the continued presence of Israeli forces depends on Hezbollah's disarmament status. These remarks were reported by an Iran International journalist.

Heavy vehicle drivers reported a halt and uncertainty at the Pishin border terminal in Rask county. Their follow-ups with the customs head have so far been unsuccessful. They are calling for urgent intervention by authorities to resolve the issue.
A citizen reported to Iran International that the drug Tiotropium prescribed for their lung disease is not available with insurance and must be purchased on the free market for 1.7 million tomans.

Arshia Barari, a 22-year-old karateka and fitness champion, was killed during the protests of Dey 1404. He was a representative of the Kyokushin style and a self-defense coach in Zanjan province. He was also an official trainer of search and rescue dogs.

Mohammad Akrami-Nia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic of Iran Army, stated that Tehran's military doctrine has shifted toward "preemptive operations." Operation "Thunderbolt" was carried out in three stages using Fath missiles and Arash-2 drones equipped with artificial intelligence, targeting American bases from Jordan to the UAE. He emphasized that they will stand firm until the Americans leave the region.

Canada's Foreign Ministry condemned the threats by the Iranian Armed Forces spokesperson against journalists abroad. The ministry emphasized strong support for the right of media to operate. Canada considers media freedom an essential part of democratic societies.

A truck driver complained in a video to Iran International about the rising prices of vehicle spare parts and the reduction of fuel quotas for drivers. He said fuel prices increase daily but their quotas are reduced. He also mentioned neglect of drivers' rights.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, the head coach of Esteghlal, removed Saleh Hardani from training due to a dispute with Yaser Asani over taking free kicks. The decision was made after the argument continued between the two players in the locker room. Bakhtiarizadeh has requested Hardani to apologize to the coaching staff and teammates for his return to training.

Keyvan Khosravani, a famous Iranian artist and designer, passed away at the age of 88 in France. He was among the first to combine traditional Iranian art and handicrafts with modern design. His notable works include designing official Iranian dignitaries' clothing and the Nayin guesthouse in Isfahan.

Mohammad Nabi Mousavi-Fard, the Friday prayer leader of Ahvaz, stated that the Islamic Republic has full control over regional movements and will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He emphasized that Iran's resolve to cut off America's influence in the region is strong and unbreakable. He also said that the Iranian people will stand firm against any excess demands.

The head of the National Pharmacists Association announced that the country faces a shortage of about 400 types of medicine. Among these, 90 essential medicines have a definite shortage and 20 medicines are completely unavailable. Economic problems and the removal of preferential currency are the main reasons for these shortages.

A person's story about crying due to inability to buy a pair of shoes has received widespread reactions on social media. Users have written about the pressure of inflation and reduced purchasing power. Ayah Dris reports on users' reactions and their stories.

Matin Parvizi, 22 years old, was killed by a gunshot in Zanjan on January 8, 2026. His mother lit a candle for him in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." She hopes his name will be remembered in history.

Donald Trump claimed that three main nuclear sites of the Islamic Republic have been completely destroyed in the war between the US and Iran. Washington is monitoring activities at these sites and Kuh-e-Kalang from space. These statements were made more than six months after the start of the war.
A citizen posted a video showing the emptiness of the computer market in Noor Passage, Tehran. He said he had never seen the market like this before. The market is very slow.

The Minister of Education emphasized the continuation of in-person schooling even during wartime. He stated that Iranian schools will continue in-person activities even under the most severe conditions. The enemy aims to shut down education in the country.

Hossein Ali Shahriari said that repaying Iran's debt in the form of food and medicine is wrong and Iran should decide on its financial resources. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic and the IRGC Navy will remain in control of the Strait of Hormuz and will not allow any new passage to be created. Shahriari also stated that the Islamic Republic will not give up its right to nuclear enrichment.

In the past week, 22 illegal hunters and wood traffickers were arrested, and over 6 hectares of natural resources were affected by fire. The air quality index in 31 cities was declared unhealthy and dangerous. Drought crisis, waste, and pollutants were also reported as other environmental issues.

The US, along with the UK, France, and Germany, is seeking to pass a resolution at the IAEA Board of Governors to report Iran's nuclear violations to the UN Security Council. This resolution follows a previous one that accused Iran of incomplete cooperation. The resolution is set to be approved one day before Israeli attacks on Iran's nuclear sites.

In Iran, videos are being shared where people state the prices of their purchases and then dance. The prices are very high, close to half of the minimum monthly wage. Some individuals say they smile out of fear of accusations and punishment.

Parsa Najafi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Isfahan, remains in indefinite detention in Dastgerd prison three months after his arrest. He is deprived of contact and visitation with his family. His family has no information about his condition.

Ahmad Motahari-Asl, the Friday prayer leader of Tabriz, said in the Friday sermon that weaknesses of the country should not be expressed in a way that encourages the enemy and discourages the people. He added that people see the economic problems but remain loyal to the country, the revolution, and the system.

The complete score of the special anthem for the 2500-year celebration of the Iranian monarchy has been published for the first time. Music researcher Pejman Akbarzadeh released this document. The written version of the anthem was found in an archive in Tehran.

Alhurra network reported a plan to deliver weapons of armed groups affiliated with the Islamic Republic to the Popular Mobilization Forces instead of the Iraqi government is under review. The military spokesman of the Iraqi Prime Minister confirmed these weapons will be reorganized after delivery. More details were provided by the Iran International reporter.

Artin Ghazanfari, a Baha'i citizen and photojournalist, has been held indefinitely in Tehran's Great Prison for over seven months. He suffers from heart disease, asthma, and high blood pressure and has been deprived of proper medical care. His family's efforts to secure his temporary release for treatment have been unsuccessful.

Scott Bassett stated that the Islamic Republic has not exported any oil in the past month and a half and currently has neither exports nor imports. He said the US will take new action on Tuesday, September 7, and more banks may be sanctioned. The Treasury Secretary described Iran's economic situation as critical and said US allies support this policy.

The Human Rights Organization for Sports expressed concern in a letter to the International Equestrian Federation and the Asian Equestrian Confederation about the situation of Taraneh Rahimi. Taraneh Rahimi, 20 years old, was arrested on January 8, 2026, in Isfahan, and the Revolutionary Court of Isfahan issued a death sentence for her on August 30. This issue was raised by Zahra Abdollahkhani, a researcher in international sports policies.
Several missiles were launched from Isfahan at different times today. The sound of missile launches has been reported. This event has been announced by local sources.

The British institution Pearson announced that due to new US sanctions, PTE language tests and Australian medical exams for residents of Iran have been canceled. This decision has been effective since September 8, 2026, and candidates must provide proof of residence outside Iran. This affects students and doctors intending to migrate.

Diesel prices in the United States have reached a new record, exceeding five and a half dollars per gallon. The American Automobile Association announced on Friday, September 4th, that the price of diesel in the country has now reached five dollars and eighty-five cents per gallon. The association attributed this price increase to disruptions in fuel transportation due to the war between the US and Iran.

Disputes between Iran and the US have intensified over the future of the Strait of Hormuz. The US has rejected returning to the Islamabad memorandum and demands a new agreement. Iran seeks to revive the agreement to reduce tensions and resume oil transit.

Mehdi Moslehi explained that delivering Iranian oil thousands of kilometers away from the Persian Gulf does not necessarily mean fresh shipments are passing through maritime routes. Some of Iran's oil was previously stored in floating tanks or Asian ports. Now, it is delivered to customers through ship-to-ship transfers and document changes.

Reports indicate a significant increase in demand among citizens for collecting vegetable waste, spotted fruits, and even partially moldy fruits. Some fruit sellers describe this scene as a daily occurrence. More details are provided in an interview with Samira Rahi.

Rescuers in Nepal saved one survivor nine days after an ice, rock, and mudslide in a tunnel connected to a hydropower plant on the Trishuli River. The incident occurred on Wednesday, 4 Shahrivar, trapping at least 900 people in the tunnels. The Nepal Army released a video of the rescue operation.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, stated that the president's perspective is feminine and maternal, paying special attention to soft areas. She added that the presence of four women in the cabinet has highlighted issues such as details of social groups, the environment, and social matters.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated in the Friday prayer sermon in Mashhad that the main strategy of the system is resistance and struggle. He emphasized that there should be no negotiations regarding nuclear technology. He also noted that the enemy no longer discusses nuclear issues in the negotiations to end the war.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, explained the image where she showed a heart with her hand. She said the heart she showed looked like a kidney and after learning from her niece, she did it again. She also responded to criticisms about this behavior and questioned why it should not be done in an official setting.

Mojtaba Khamenei announced in the Government Week message that any act harming social cohesion is forbidden. However, in a regime where factions accuse each other, this order is quickly violated. Implementing this order requires a ruler who can impose costs for disobedience, but Mojtaba Khamenei lacks his father's political background and influence.

Canada's Foreign Ministry condemned the threats against Iranian journalists abroad by the spokesperson of the Islamic Republic's armed forces. The ministry emphasized strong support for the right of media to operate freely and independently. This report was prepared by Mahsa Mortazavi.

In Iran, governmental methods to control citizens' behavior before actions occur have increased. These methods include summons, warnings, obtaining commitments, and threats of closure aimed at changing future behavior. This shift indicates a move from punishment after the act to preventive control of behaviors.

Al Arabiya reported that missiles launched from Iran were intercepted in northern Jordan. Images of the interception have been released. Earlier, channels close to the IRGC stated that missiles were launched from Isfahan, Kerman, and Kermanshah.

The US sanctioned Golden Global Bank and two affiliated companies in Turkey for facilitating tens of millions of dollars transfers for the Quds Force of the IRGC. The US Treasury described this as part of the 'economic expulsion' operation to cut off financial resources of the Islamic Republic. The bank enabled the transfer of Iran's oil revenues from China to Turkey.

A group of Iranians living in Germany gathered in Hamburg on Friday, 13 Shahrivar. The gathering was in protest against the executions by the Islamic Republic. Videos of this gathering have been sent to Iran International.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, stated on X that China seeks to strengthen common security, an approach supported by the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that regional countries should work to establish a regional security structure. Ghalibaf added that the Islamic Republic is ready to cooperate in this effort.

The US, UK, France, and Germany are negotiating to pass a resolution in the IAEA Board of Governors to report Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council. This follows a resolution from June accusing Iran of incomplete cooperation. Iran has not allowed inspectors to visit bombed nuclear sites.

The US State Department announced that the United States remains committed to cutting off the Islamic Republic's access to the international financial system and resources that it says are used to destabilize the region and threaten US interests and partners. The department said sanctions on Turkey-based Golden Global Bank are the latest action under the Economic Exclusion Operation and that facilitating Iran's illegal financial activities will have serious consequences. Washington said it will continue using diplomatic and economic tools to isolate the Islamic Republic until it stops supporting terrorism and destabilizing activities in the region.

Saman Taherpour said Keyvan Khosravani was one of the founders of combining modernism with authentic Iranian art and tradition. Khosravani introduced this approach to the world with the collaboration of Empress Farah. He used traditional Iranian arts in designing the official dresses of Empress Farah.

Axios, citing American officials and informed sources, reported that the Trump administration is developing a post-war strategy for Iran aimed at containing Iran and expanding normalization of Israel's relations with regional countries. Trump has held two meetings with senior advisors in recent weeks and has said in private conversations that he is working on 'something much bigger' in the Middle East. The three main pillars of the plan include regional alignment to contain Iran, advancing the next phase of the Gaza plan, and reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria and implementing the Israel-Lebanon agreement.

Alireza Arafi stated that the US is unfamiliar with Iran's asymmetric and guerrilla warfare methods. He also mentioned the global hatred towards the US due to its oppressive actions. These remarks were made in Qom.

Donald Trump stated that there are no naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and that the US lost no personnel in its operation in Venezuela. He mentioned that the US might soon target 'Kuh Kolang Gazla' and that 18 people were killed in the conflict with Iran. Trump also said the US targeted the Islamic Republic's radars for the second time.

A woman in Tehran accused of acid attack on her landlord was sentenced to 15 years in prison and payment of blood money. The sentence was issued by the criminal court of Tehran province. More details were published by Harana News Agency.

Niloufar Majaver, a 27-year-old woman from Piranshahr, died after several days of hospitalization and being declared brain dead. Her family reported physical and sexual violence and deprivation of food and water before her hospital transfer. A complaint has been filed against a person related to the case, but no arrests have been made yet.

The audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad discusses the empty docks of Iranian ports following US economic sanctions. This issue is presented as an economic challenge for Iran. The program examines the effects of these sanctions.

Research by Program 24 shows a sharp decline in activity at Shahid Rajaee and Imam Khomeini ports. Shahid Rajaee port, handling 85% of Iran's container trade, has been most affected. Increased insurance costs and the naval blockade have reduced commercial ship traffic.

Romania's Ministry of Defense announced the neutralization of an explosive device from a drone in the Black Sea. The bomb disposal team carried out the operation about five nautical miles east of the Sulina branch entrance. Romania, Bulgaria, and Turkey have neutralized over 150 drifting mines in the Black Sea and expanded their joint mine-clearing force.

Donald Trump mentioned the possibility of an attack on Mount Kalang Gezla, a site of important nuclear activities of the Islamic Republic. A military expert said the US can target the deep facilities in this area using bunker-buster bombs and B-2 aircraft. The expert also noted that missile attacks by the Islamic Republic on Jordan might push Jordan closer to the US.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that the Islamic Republic is under full sanctions and facing economic death. He said Washington intends to economically strangle the Islamic Republic. US allies in the Persian Gulf and Europe also support this policy.

The Israeli army announced the clearance of tunnels leading to the Ali Al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon. It was reported that members of the IRGC are present in the area alongside Hezbollah forces. Additionally, the Islamic Republic has warned the US via Oman about Israel's capture of this area.

The spokesperson of Qatar's Foreign Ministry rejected the Islamic Republic's narrative about the attacks on Qatar, stating that official UN documents show Iranian missiles targeted civilian areas. Qatar's letters to the UN recorded damages and injuries. The spokesperson also confirmed the attack on Ras Laffan gas facilities and denied calling it an "alleged" attack.

Donald Trump stated that the US military may soon target underground facilities at Mount Kalang-Gazla in Iran. At the same time, the IRGC launched missile attacks on Jordan. The Trump administration is developing a strategic plan for the post-war period with the Islamic Republic.

The US has simultaneously sanctioned a bank and two Turkish financial companies. Siamak Javadi stated that the US is targeting the financial architecture of the Islamic Republic through secondary sanctions. These measures may lead to reduced foreign currency revenues and increased pressure on Iran's economy.

Ata Mohamad said that Israel's capture of Ali Al-Taher hill reduces Hezbollah's operational capabilities and gives Israel military superiority. This development may increase pressure on the Lebanese government to disarm Hezbollah. It also raises the likelihood of a long-term Israeli presence in the southern Lebanon buffer zone.

The 107th derby between Esteghlal and Persepolis was the first match between the two teams after the massacre of the Iranian people on January 8 and 9, 2026. Many martyrs of January were supporters of these two teams. Mazdak Mirzaei interviewed Mohammad Taghavi on the Hat-trick program.

Niloufar Majaver, a 27-year-old woman from Piranshahr, died after 10 days of severe physical and sexual abuse in an unknown location. Her family has filed a complaint against Ezzatodin Seyed Taheri, who is accused of the crime but has not been arrested yet. Reports indicate that this individual has abused other women as well.

Niloufar Majaver, a young woman from Piranshahr and Oshnavieh, was transferred to a hospital with severe injuries 10 days after leaving home and died from brain death. Her family holds a 41-year-old man responsible, but official investigations have not confirmed this. Reports differ on the details of the incident and Niloufar's personal information.

CENTCOM announced that US paratroopers have deployed communication equipment in a remote location in the Middle East. The exact location of the deployment was not disclosed. This action coincides with the ongoing extensive US military presence in the region.

Yemen's legitimate government forces have regained control of Saeed Taher Hill and the Dhayban area in Hayfan district from the Houthis. Military positions in the Al-Tuwair front in Taiz province were also recaptured, and the air force bombed Houthi positions. The Yemeni army reported that hundreds of Houthi militants were killed and wounded on the western coast.

TankersTrackers identified 17 ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil and gas in the Gulf of Oman on Friday. At least 24 million barrels of oil and petroleum products were moved in these transfers. Additionally, more oil tankers are waiting in the area to find other ships for transfer operations.

More than 120 people have been killed in Yemen after Houthi forces launched an operation to advance towards the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The clashes began with a ground attack supported by missile and drone strikes near the Red Sea coast. The Houthis are trying to strengthen their positions in this area.

On Friday evening, part of Kazemi Street in Isfahan subsided as a tanker passed. The tanker's wheels fell into the created hole. Firefighters and the water and sewage company managed to remove the tanker from the hole.

Two labor organizations condemned the shooting of job-seeking youth in Gachsaran and Ahvaz in a joint statement. They described the incident as part of labor suppression and widespread unemployment. They also warned that poverty and unemployment have become a serious crisis.

The New York Times reported that US government inspectors subjected about 50 members of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to lie detector tests in connection with leaks to journalists. The tests were conducted in August following reports of shortages of key munitions. A Pentagon spokesman declined to comment on the investigation but said the department takes leaks of classified information seriously.

Shahram Khaledi mentioned the possibility of a US attack on the Kooh Kalang nuclear site. He said the impact of such an attack depends on how it is carried out. Destroying underground equipment may require many bunker-buster bombs or special forces.

The drone war between Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea has changed the security measures of ships. Oil tankers and cargo ships use nets and water tanks for protection. Ankara has entered negotiations with Russia and Ukraine to ensure maritime security in the region.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi stated that the US, UK, France, and Germany are trying to refer Iran's nuclear file back to the UN Security Council. He said this move is mostly symbolic and political. Practically, it will not bring any new measures beyond existing resolutions and sanctions.

Daneshjoo news agency reported that a small Islamic Republic oil tanker was attacked on Khark Island. The attack was carried out by the US military with a missile. There were no casualties, and no other sources have confirmed the report yet.
